what_its_for: Miglustat is used to treat a rare genetic condition called Gaucher disease (type 1) in adults who cannot use enzyme replacement therapy. It works by reducing the buildup of fatty substances (glucosylceramide) in your body that cause the disease. It may also be used for another rare condition called Niemann-Pick type C disease.
how_to_take: Take miglustat capsules by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or chew it. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember. It is usually taken three times a day (morning, afternoon, and evening).
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 100 mg capsule taken three times daily. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have kidney problems or if you experience bothersome side effects like diarrhea or tremor (shaking). Always follow the dose your doctor prescribes — do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store miglustat capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the container tightly closed and away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while taking miglustat — it can harm an unborn baby. Women should use reliable birth control during treatment and for 3 months after stopping. Men should also use a barrier method of contraception (such as a condom) during treatment and for 3 months after stopping, as miglustat may affect sperm. Avoid foods high in dairy or certain carbohydrates if they worsen your diarrhea, as this medicine commonly causes loose stools especially early in treatment. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe or persistent diarrhea or stomach pain; numbness, tingling, or burning in your hands or feet (nerve problems); uncontrolled shaking or tremors that interfere with daily life; memory problems, confusion, or difficulty with coordination; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness; or if you are trying to become pregnant or think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Miglustat works gradually over time. Some improvements, such as reduced organ size (liver and spleen) and better blood counts, may be noticed after several months of regular treatment. It is important to keep taking it even if you do not feel different right away. Your doctor will check your progress with regular blood tests and exams.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use miglustat if you are pregnant — it can seriously harm the baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Miglustat is generally not recommended for children with Gaucher disease. It may be used in children with Niemann-Pick type C disease under close medical supervision. Kidney problems: Your dose may need to be lowered if your kidneys do not work well — tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Elderly: Older adults may need extra monitoring for side effects such as tremor and nerve problems.
